sources.entry: oracledb - The official Python driver for Oracle Database, successor to cx_Oracle.

summary.one_liner: python-oracledb is the official, Oracle-maintained Python driver for connecting to Oracle Database, and the successor to the obsolete cx_Oracle driver.
summary.what_it_does: The driver conforms to the Python Database API 2.0 specification with additions, and is built with Cython. It runs in a default 'Thin' mode that connects directly to Oracle Database without extra libraries, or in 'Thick' mode when optional Oracle Client libraries are loaded for advanced functionality. The README lists support for SQL and PL/SQL execution, data frames, fast data ingestion, NoSQL-style document APIs, message queueing, database notifications, and starting and stopping the database. It also mentions high availability and security features, synchronous and concurrent coding styles, and optional pipelining of database operations. An optional embedded OpenTelemetry plugin can be enabled explicitly, which emits the db.client.operation.duration metric when a MeterProvider is configured.
use_cases: connect a Python program to Oracle Database
run SQL and PL/SQL statements from Python
bulk or fast data loading into Oracle tables
add OpenTelemetry tracing to Oracle database calls
migrate legacy cx_Oracle code to a maintained driver
how_to_run: Set user, password and DSN, then call oracledb.connect(user=un, password=pw, dsn=cs)
Run the basic example: cursor.execute("select sysdate from dual")
stack: Oracle Instant Client (optional, for Thick mode)
notable: Thin mode needs no Oracle Client libraries; Thick mode is optional
Conforms to Python DB API 2.0 with a feature list of additions
Supports synchronous and concurrent coding styles and pipelining
Optional embedded OpenTelemetry plugin that must be enabled explicitly
Maintained by Oracle and succeeds cx_Oracle
caveats: Thin mode requires Oracle Database 12.1 or later; Thick mode requires 11.2 or later depending on client release
Some advanced functionality is only available in Thick mode with Oracle Client libraries installed
Do not run the OpenTelemetry plugin alongside other Oracle or DBAPI OpenTelemetry instrumentation in the same process
